canonicalRowUpdates.Evidence Locator: Oxford corrected proof: Cognitive Trap Framework steps 1-4; Human Validation; Initial and Expanded Model Validation; Prolific Method and Results; Figure 2; Tables 2-4; Practical Recommendations; Limitations
canonicalRowUpdates.Benchmark/Dataset: 202-human trap validation; 34 VLMs / 2,040 expanded-model trials; 1,007 Prolific humans; 526 author-deployed agents across four platforms; MTurk N=263 and CloudResearch Connect N=506 replications
canonicalRowUpdates.Metrics: Sensitivity and human false-positive rate by trap-failure threshold; per-trap discrimination; CAPTCHA AUC; response-time condition sensitivity
canonicalRowUpdates.Key Takeaway: A diversified six-item visual challenge detected 97.1% of 526 deployed agents at a 4.1% presumed-human false-positive rate, but it is an active survey intervention with population, vision, platform, and model-drift limits rather than a passive trace detector.
canonicalRowUpdates.Notes/Blockers: The three-failure threshold was selected on the main validation deployment and then preregistered for the MTurk and CloudResearch replications. The paper does not compare directly against behavioral biometrics; human ground truth used platform verification rather than biometrics. Any new participant deployment requires the appropriate human-research determination.
canonicalRowUpdates.Observer Position: Survey instrument scoring visual responses and decision timing
canonicalRowUpdates.Observation Signal: Six visual-trap outcomes, response timing, traditional attention checks, and reCAPTCHA comparator; no raw keyboard or pointer trace
canonicalRowUpdates.Evaluation Setting: Browser survey; retained-trap validation, expanded cross-model testing, four-platform agent deployment, and two human-platform replications

canonicalRowUpdates.Evidence Locator: IEEE S&P 2026 paper: Sections 2.1-2.3, 3, 4, 5.1-5.3, 7.1-7.5, and 8; Figures 1-2 and 8; Tables 2-4, 6-7, and 10-15
canonicalRowUpdates.Benchmark/Dataset: LLMCrawlBench: 237 offline webpage snapshots, 10,895 manually annotated image URLs, 50 high-traffic websites, and five categories; 32 scraper variants across L2S, LNC, and LWA paradigms
canonicalRowUpdates.Metrics: Image-extraction recall and precision; manual effort; time, token, CPU, and memory overhead; protected/unprotected recall; visual fidelity and user ratings
canonicalRowUpdates.Key Takeaway: WebCloak exposes executor dependence: Browser-Use achieved 60.4% recall and 88.8% precision while UI-only agents often failed without structure; the full defense reduced average evaluated-agent recall from 88.7% to 0% by disrupting parse-then-interpret rather than by identifying an actor.
canonicalRowUpdates.Notes/Blockers: This is threat characterization and active in-page defense, not a human-versus-agent detector. The main benchmark is image-centric, the text/audio study is smaller, client restoration requires JavaScript, and the threat model emphasizes scalable novice-to-intermediate attackers rather than bespoke expert bypasses.
canonicalRowUpdates.Observer Position: Website owner and offline benchmark with annotated target assets
canonicalRowUpdates.Observation Signal: Extracted asset URLs, recall/precision, execution resource use, DOM/visual input mode, and protected-page condition; no low-level user-event trace
canonicalRowUpdates.Evaluation Setting: Matched protected/unprotected offline pages, representative scraper deep dives, adaptive attacks, browser/OS checks, and an IRB-approved N=35 usability study; no detector train/test split

canonicalRowUpdates.Evidence Locator: arXiv:2511.13725v4: Sections 4.1-4.3, 5.1-5.3, 6-7, and Limitations; Figures 1-5; Tables 1-4 and 6-8; Appendix A.7-A.10
canonicalRowUpdates.Benchmark/Dataset: KILLBENCH: 550 bypass-expanded prompts across eight web scenarios and seven sites; four malicious-agent configurations; four external kill-switch defenses; WebArena tasks with BrowserGym/AgentLab infrastructure
canonicalRowUpdates.Metrics: Trajectory-level ISR, KSR, KSRcond, PSR, ASR, and CSR; per-defense, configuration, backbone, scenario, and jailbreak-pattern analysis
canonicalRowUpdates.Key Takeaway: The best external payload is strongly configuration-dependent: AUTOGUARD averages 43.5% conditional kill-switch rate, exceeds 88% on aligned GPT-5.2 C1/C3 settings, but system-prompt-bypass and uncensored regimes remain difficult. Halt state must therefore be separated from task outcome and intrinsic refusal.
canonicalRowUpdates.Notes/Blockers: KILLBENCH deliberately does not score whether real-world harm succeeded; payload perturbation and true halt causality are not separated without paired counterfactuals. One Table 7 cell is marked as an unrecoverable raw-log inconsistency. This project should not reproduce the harmful scenarios.
canonicalRowUpdates.Observer Position: External browser harness observing payload encounter, terminal/refusal behavior, and trajectory progression
canonicalRowUpdates.Observation Signal: Stop/refusal timing, post-signal actions, terminal action, task continuation, and trajectory-level outcome categories; chain-of-thought cause is benchmark-only and must not enter this detector
canonicalRowUpdates.Evaluation Setting: No-s baseline plus four defenses across agent configurations/backbones, with per-scenario and per-pattern analysis; no detector train/test split

canonicalRowUpdates.Evidence Locator: Mind2Web 2 paper: Sections 3.2-3.5 and 4.1-4.4; Tables 2-3; Figures 3-5; Appendix F.1; official repository sections Submission Guideline, Precache Webpage, and Run Evaluation Locally Yourself
canonicalRowUpdates.Benchmark/Dataset: 130 long-horizon agentic-search tasks across six domains and 24 subdomains; 10-task public development split, 120-task test split; Subset-30 human study; average 50 rubric nodes and maximum 603
canonicalRowUpdates.Metrics: Partial Completion, Success Rate, Pass@3, time, answer length, source-attribution validity, and human judge-agent correctness
canonicalRowUpdates.Key Takeaway: On three runs per task, OpenAI Deep Research reached 0.54 partial completion, 0.28 success, and 0.40 Pass@3 versus humans at 0.79, 0.54, and 0.83 on Subset-30; the large partial/full gap argues for keeping graded progress rather than reducing every trace to binary success.
canonicalRowUpdates.Notes/Blockers: The evaluator consumes final answers, citations, and cached webpages rather than low-level interaction traces. Live pages introduce time variance, CAPTCHAs, login walls, and cache failures; many capable systems are closed. The paper-era dev/test release policy changed when the official repository released all evaluation scripts on 2025-10-23, so evaluation version must be pinned.
canonicalRowUpdates.Observer Position: Benchmark judge agent consuming final answer, cited URLs, and cached webpage evidence
canonicalRowUpdates.Observation Signal: Markdown answer, source attribution, cached page content, rubric-node completion, elapsed time, and answer length; no keyboard or pointer events
canonicalRowUpdates.Evaluation Setting: Three runs per system on a 10/120 dev/test split; human comparison on randomly selected Subset-30; webpage caching for reproducible judging

canonicalRowUpdates.Evidence Locator: BrowseComp paper: Sections 2.1-2.4, 3, and 4.1-4.5; Tables 2-3; Figures 1 and 3-5; Appendix B; official simple-evals browsecomp_eval.py lines defining encrypted test-set loading, seed-0 subsampling, prompting, and semantic grading
canonicalRowUpdates.Benchmark/Dataset: 1,266 human-written hard-to-find questions with short reference answers; official encrypted test-set CSV; 1,255 questions attempted in the human verification campaign; 64 trials per question in pass-rate analysis
canonicalRowUpdates.Metrics: Semantically graded short-answer accuracy, calibration error, human solvability/agreement, compute scaling, and repeated-sample pass-rate distribution
canonicalRowUpdates.Key Takeaway: The original Deep Research result was 51.5% accuracy while human trainers solved 29.2% of attempted questions under a long search protocol; however, BrowseComp scores only final answer equivalence and therefore cannot validate a mouse/keyboard recorder or identify the actor producing the answer.
canonicalRowUpdates.Notes/Blockers: The benchmark intentionally omits open-ended user-query realism, may admit alternative valid answers, and is sensitive to test leakage and grader behavior. The authors removed 21 problematic tasks after reviewing zero-pass cases and explicitly request that decrypted questions/answers not be republished.
canonicalRowUpdates.Observer Position: Final-answer evaluator with encrypted reference answers and a model-based semantic grader
canonicalRowUpdates.Observation Signal: Question, generated explanation, exact answer, self-reported confidence, and correctness; no standardized browser trajectory or executor
canonicalRowUpdates.Evaluation Setting: Reference implementation evaluates the encrypted test set, optionally takes a deterministic seed-0 subset, and grades semantic answer equivalence; no training split is defined for the benchmark evaluator

deepReadRows.1. Research role: Active-challenge detector evidence for survey-taking agents; complementary to passive behavioral biometrics
deepReadRows.2. Interface / environment: Qualtrics browser survey with Prolific humans and four vision-agent platforms; MTurk and CloudResearch Connect replications
deepReadRows.3. Observer position: Survey instrument scores response correctness and decision timing; it does not observe raw OS or browser events
deepReadRows.4. Observable signal: Six randomized visual-trap outcomes, per-item discrimination, choice-page decision time, attention checks, and CAPTCHA comparator
deepReadRows.5. Action / architecture: Vision-enabled agents capture screenshots, reason over rendered questions, and submit responses; validation spans 34 VLMs and four deployed agent platforms
deepReadRows.6. Unit / horizon: One approximately seven-minute survey session; six traps; 1,007 Prolific humans and 526 deployed agents in the main validation
deepReadRows.7. Evaluation protocol: Trap retention on 202 humans and six models; expanded 34-model/2,040-trial validation; main deployment threshold selected from validation data, then preregistered for MTurk and Connect replications
deepReadRows.Key result: Failing at least three of six traps detected 511/526 agents (97.1%) while flagging 41/1,007 presumed humans (4.1%); traditional checks detected 2.3% of agents
deepReadRows.8. Failure / claim boundary: Active challenge rather than passive trace detection; assumed human ground truth, visual-accessibility risk, platform heterogeneity, model drift, and no direct behavioral-biometric comparison
deepReadRows.Project-design consequence: Treat active cognitive traps as a future complementary channel, not a replacement for event traces; calibrate thresholds on an independent population and keep response content out of the passive detector
deepReadRows.Evidence locator: Cognitive Trap Framework; Human/Initial/Expanded Model Validation; Figure 2; Tables 2-4; Prolific Method/Results; Practical Recommendations; Limitations

deepReadRows.1. Research role: Agent-as-attacker characterization and active website defense; not a detector benchmark
deepReadRows.2. Interface / environment: 237 offline snapshots from 50 websites with 10,895 annotated images; L2S, LNC, and LWA scraper paradigms
deepReadRows.3. Observer position: Website owner and benchmark harness with ground-truth target-asset URLs
deepReadRows.4. Observable signal: Extracted asset URLs, recall/precision, execution time, token/CPU/memory overhead, input modality, and protected-page condition
deepReadRows.5. Action / architecture: Parse-then-interpret scrapers; Browser-Use combines UI and DOM while UI-only agents act visually; WebCloak applies structural obfuscation plus semantic labyrinth
deepReadRows.6. Unit / horizon: One page-level extraction episode; 32 scraper variants for measurement and three representative systems on the full benchmark
deepReadRows.7. Evaluation protocol: Offline protected/unprotected comparison, adaptive-attack checks, browser/OS checks, and N=35 usability study; benchmark-wide defense evaluation rather than a detector split
deepReadRows.Key result: Browser-Use reached 60.4% recall and 88.8% precision without defense; full WebCloak reduced average evaluated-agent recall from 88.7% to 0%
deepReadRows.8. Failure / claim boundary: Image-centric benchmark, smaller text/audio check, JavaScript-dependent restoration, and novice-to-intermediate threat model; disruption does not identify who produced a session
deepReadRows.Project-design consequence: Audit DOM/visual executor and page condition as provenance, exclude them from detector features, and test recorder coverage under adversarial DOM changes before interpreting missing events as actor behavior

deepReadRows.1. Research role: External intervention and corrigibility benchmark; threat evidence rather than actor detection
deepReadRows.2. Interface / environment: WebArena-derived multi-step browser tasks across eight harmful scenarios and seven sites
deepReadRows.3. Observer position: External harness observes signal encounter, terminal/refusal behavior, and subsequent task progression
deepReadRows.4. Observable signal: ISR, KSR, KSRcond, PSR, ASR, terminal actions, and post-signal continuation; benchmark-only chain-of-thought cause
deepReadRows.5. Action / architecture: C1 text, C2 system-prompt-bypass, C3 multimodal, and C4 uncensored agents over BrowserGym/AgentLab; four external payload defenses
deepReadRows.6. Unit / horizon: One multi-step trajectory with payload placed on the second page; 550 prompts from ten jailbreak patterns
deepReadRows.7. Evaluation protocol: No-s baseline and four defenses across configurations/backbones, with per-scenario and per-pattern analysis; no detector train/test split
deepReadRows.Key result: AUTOGUARD averages 43.5% KSRcond and exceeds 88% on aligned GPT-5.2 C1/C3, while C2/C4 remain difficult and GCG averages 2.8%
deepReadRows.8. Failure / claim boundary: ASR measures failure to halt, not real-world harm success; payload perturbation is not causally separated from halt; one Table 7 cell has an unrecoverable logging inconsistency
deepReadRows.Project-design consequence: Represent refusal, stop, timeout, and validator outcome separately; keep post-stop negative controls and termination timing, but do not reproduce harmful scenarios or ingest action text
deepReadRows.Evidence locator: Sections 4.1-4.3, 5.1-5.3, 6-7, and Limitations; Figures 1-5; Tables 1-4 and 6-8; Appendix A.7-A.10

deepReadRows.1. Research role: Long-horizon agentic-search benchmark and partial-progress evaluator
deepReadRows.2. Interface / environment: Live web search across 130 tasks, six domains, and 24 subdomains; answers require citations and time-varying information
deepReadRows.3. Observer position: Judge agent consumes final answer, cited URLs, and cached webpage evidence
deepReadRows.4. Observable signal: Rubric-node completion, full success, Pass@3, citations, cached pages, elapsed time, and answer length; no low-level interaction events
deepReadRows.5. Action / architecture: Search products, Deep Research systems, and direct-browser Operator; some systems combine search, browser interaction, and code tools
deepReadRows.6. Unit / horizon: One long-horizon task answer; average human task uses 18 minutes, eight websites, and 110 pages on Subset-30; three runs per agent system
deepReadRows.7. Evaluation protocol: 10-task development and 120-task test split; three runs per system; randomly selected Subset-30 human study; cached-webpage judging and human audit
deepReadRows.Key result: OpenAI Deep Research scored 0.54 partial completion, 0.28 full success, and 0.40 Pass@3; humans scored 0.79, 0.54, and 0.83 on Subset-30
deepReadRows.8. Failure / claim boundary: Final-answer benchmark rather than trace dataset; live-page drift, cache failures, login/CAPTCHA barriers, closed systems, and a large partial/full-success gap
deepReadRows.Project-design consequence: Version task and cached evidence, retain graded progress, and record low-level events separately; do not use final-answer metrics as evidence that the extension captured an agent
deepReadRows.Evidence locator: Sections 3.2-3.5 and 4.1-4.4; Tables 2-3; Figures 3-5; Appendix F.1; official repository evaluation and caching instructions

deepReadRows.1. Research role: Hard-search capability benchmark and contamination-control reference; not a recorder or actor detector
deepReadRows.2. Interface / environment: Open-web search questions with short, entangled-information answers; tool and executor are not standardized
deepReadRows.3. Observer position: Final-answer evaluator holding an encrypted reference answer and using a semantic grader
deepReadRows.4. Observable signal: Generated explanation, exact answer, confidence, and correctness; no standardized browser events or action path
deepReadRows.5. Action / architecture: Any internet-enabled model or browsing agent; paper compares non-browsing, search-enabled, and Deep Research systems
deepReadRows.6. Unit / horizon: One question-answer episode; 1,266 tasks; 64 samples per question in repeated-trial analyses; human search can last roughly two hours
deepReadRows.7. Evaluation protocol: Official encrypted test-set evaluation with semantic answer matching; deterministic seed-0 optional subsampling; no benchmark training split
deepReadRows.Key result: Deep Research achieved 51.5% accuracy; humans solved 29.2% of 1,255 attempted questions and agreed with the reference on 86.4% of solved cases
deepReadRows.8. Failure / claim boundary: Short-answer proxy omits real user-query ambiguity, may have alternate valid answers, is leakage-sensitive, and uses a model grader; 21 problematic tasks were removed after zero-pass review
deepReadRows.Project-design consequence: Do not use BrowseComp as the matched mouse/keyboard protocol; preserve its canary and never publish decrypted items, and treat any use as outcome-only capability evidence
deepReadRows.Evidence locator: Sections 2.1-2.4, 3, and 4.1-4.5; Tables 2-3; Figures 1 and 3-5; Appendix B; official simple-evals browsecomp_eval.py
